aspects.says: Code that closes several resources itself closes the newest first and keeps closing the others after one fails.
basis: section:Resources Close in Reverse Order, Before the Statement's catch and finally Run
section:A close() Failure Is Attached as Suppressed, Not Thrown in Place of the Body's Exception

aspects.says: A variable named in the header must be final or effectively final.
basis: section:A Variable Named in the Header Is Closed Too, Whoever Opened It
aspects.reason: javac enforces it, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch, and the page gives the compiler's message

aspects.says: Declared separately, a wrapped resource is closed twice; Closeable requires that to be harmless, AutoCloseable does not, so a close() of your own must be idempotent.
basis: section:Only a Resource That Finished Constructing Is Closed, So Declare Each Stream Separately

aspects.says: A suppressed close failure is reachable only through getSuppressed() or a printed stack trace; the thrown exception's message does not include it.
basis: section:A close() Failure Is Attached as Suppressed, Not Thrown in Place of the Body's Exception

aspects.says: Since Java 9 a statement can name an existing variable as a resource, and it closes that object whoever opened it.
basis: section:A Variable Named in the Header Is Closed Too, Whoever Opened It

aspects.says: Only a resource that finished constructing is closed, so a stream created inside another resource's constructor call leaks when that constructor throws; declaring each stream separately closes it.
basis: section:Only a Resource That Finished Constructing Is Closed, So Declare Each Stream Separately

aspects.says: A try-with-resources statement closes its resources in reverse order of declaration, before its own catch and finally run.
basis: section:Resources Close in Reverse Order, Before the Statement's catch and finally Run

aspects.says: When the body and a close() both throw, the body's exception is thrown and the close failure is attached to it as suppressed, where a close in finally would replace it.
basis: section:A close() Failure Is Attached as Suppressed, Not Thrown in Place of the Body's Exception
